newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-EU'S VAN MIERT WARNS UEFA ON BROADCASTING RIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EU'S VAN MIERT WARNS UEFA ON BROADCASTING RIGHTS.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warned UEFA on Thursday the Commission would act unless European soccer's governing body changed what he called strict broadcasting conditions.
"We think UEFA conditions are too strict," Van Miert told the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs committee.
"We are in discussions with UEFA, but if there is no progress we will have to act," he said, adding that the Commission had received complaints.

But UEFA spokesman Salvatore Cuccu said that UEFA and the EU were in close contact with each other regarding TV rights and but said Van Miert's warning should be regarded as part of the on-going debate.
"UEFA are working closely with the EU and a solution will be found in the next two years."

Developments in digital technology and satellite television over the past few years have revolutionised the way soccer is now broadcast around the continent, and new rules are being established to take account of the huge new developments.

Commission sources said the complaints had been filed by television channels which broadcast UEFA matches but do not have exclusivity rights. They particularly contested UEFA's sub-licensing conditions which, they said, colluded with their own interests.

Earlier this year UEFA and the EU clashed over a landmark ruling from the EU which forced UEFA to scrap its player system and transfer rules in the wake of a European Court of Justice case filed by Belgian footballer Jean-Marc Bosman.
